subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split in core, and which narrow Phase 0/1 contract should be approved first?
rationale: The request creates public runtime protocol, config, lifecycle, session-state, and security-boundary contracts that automation cannot safely choose without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve Narrow Phase 0/1 Design
options.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

options.title: Defer To Backend/Profile Slices
options.body: Use this RFC as context while maintainers review the narrower execution-backend tracker and implementation PRs first.

options.title: Pause Core Distributed Runtime Work
options.body: Do not sponsor core distributed-runtime work until Gateway stability and setup priorities move further along.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Phase 0/1 Design
recommendation.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The open worker-isolation PR and recent runtime-boundary work make this the clearest current routing candidate for the product decision.
